question.text: John couldn't recall the serial number on his new bike, but he remembered that it was $4$ digits long, each digit ranged from $0$ to $9$ and that none of the digits were used more than once. How many of these serial numbers are possible?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

\[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $10$ digits, so $n=10.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the serial number, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different $4$-digit serial numbers is

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ _{10}P_4 &= \dfrac {10!} {(10 - 4)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {10!} {6!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot \cancel{6!}} {\cancel{6!}} \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \\[5pt] &= 5\,040. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten

question.explanation:
The formula for ${}_nP_r$ is given by

\[ {}_nP_r = \dfrac {n!} {(n - r)!} \,. \]

$P(7,4)$ means the same thing as $_{7}P_4.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_nP_r,$ we get

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{P(7,4) &= \dfrac{7!}{(7-4)!}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7!}{3!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}}\\[5pt] &= 840. } \]

example.title: Calculating a Permutation Given Using Alternate Notation

question.text: Diana is choosing a $4$-digit passcode for her cellphone from the digits $\{ 1,2,3,4,5,6\},$ where no digit is used more than once. How many different passcodes are possible?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula \[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $6$ digits, so $n=6.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the passcode, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different passcodes is

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ _{6}P_4 &= \dfrac {6!} {(6 - 4)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {6!} {2!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot \cancel{2!}} {\cancel{2!}} \\[5pt] &= 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \\[5pt] &= 360. } \]
